topic: modder fixes melting RTX 5090 power connectors
headline_marked: Modder [[fixes melting RTX 5090 power connectors]] with custom distributor
headline: Modder fixes melting RTX 5090 power connectors with custom distributor
summary: A custom power distributor splits the current load across more wires to lower connector temperatures, with claims of full warranty coverage.
details: A Reddit user has shared a solution for their RTX 5090 graphics card, which was experiencing overheating power connectors. The fix involves a custom-made power distributor that splits the current load across more wires, aiming to reduce connector temperatures.

The modder, who is reportedly a partner with PNY, claims that a modified PNY-specific card with this solution could be offered directly with full warranty coverage. However, this mod is not yet available on their website, and PNY's history with warranty claims for 12VHPWR issues has been inconsistent.

The 16-pin connector issue, known as the 12VHPWR problem, affects many Nvidia graphics cards due to high current draw through a connector designed for fewer wires. Cases of melting connectors are often attributed to poor connections, high resistance, and uneven current distribution.

This mod involves soldering additional connections to the power rails directly on the RTX 5090's PCB and routing them to a custom power distributor. In stress tests, running the card at full load for 48 hours, the connector joint reportedly never exceeded 40°C.

topic: run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 125B on consumer hardware
headline_marked: [[Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B)]] AI model on consumer hardware
headline: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) AI model on consumer hardware
summary: Strata brings a large, server-grade AI model to your PC, enabling local chat, coding, and image analysis with a simple one-click install.
details: A new open-source project called Strata allows users to run the massive 125-billion-parameter Qwen 3.8 Flash Next AI model on standard consumer hardware, including PCs with NVIDIA or AMD graphics cards and 12GB of VRAM or more.

This breakthrough means that powerful AI capabilities, typically reserved for dedicated servers, can now be accessed locally on Windows or Linux machines. The model can handle tasks like chatting, writing code, and processing images, with all operations kept on the user's PC.

Performance tests show that an RTX 3090 (24GB VRAM) can achieve speeds of 100-140 tokens per second. Strata is designed for ease of use, featuring a one-click installer that automatically configures the system and downloads the approximately 70GB model.

The project leverages community-developed components and techniques to make the large model fit within the memory constraints of consumer GPUs. This includes sharing the workload across the entire PC, similar to how a kitchen might use both a counter and a pantry.

Strata is free and open-source under the MIT License, with support for development encouraged through donations. The project also integrates with AI coding assistants and offers an API for app integration.
